## Question 2

```{r Question 2}
NA & TRUE
NA & FALSE
NA | TRUE
NA | FALSE
```
<!-- ENTER YOUR EXPLANATION BELOW, FEEL FREE TO EDIT THE ABOVE CODE CHUNK -->
When there is an and, both conditions must be true in order for the function to be true--however, R does not know what NA is, it could be true or false. Therefore, it does not know if it is true or false statement. The second one is false since as long as there is one false, it remains false, and will not be true--it does not matter what NA is. When there is an or, you just need TRUE on either side, and since that is present in line 3, it outputs true. For the fourth one, NA could be true, so since it is a possibility, the output is unknown.

## Question 3

<!-- PUT YOUR get_minimum_coins() FROM HW 1 HERE -->
```{r Question 3 background} 
get_minimum_coins <- function(cents) {
  q <- cents %/% 25
  d <- (cents - (25 * q)) %/% 10
  n <- (cents - (25 * q) - (10 * d)) %/% 5
  p <- (cents - (25 * q) - (10 * d) - (5 * n)) %/% 1
  
  q + d + n + p
}
```

### (a)
<!-- ENTER YOUR ANSWER BELOW -->
Yes, this is a vectorized function because when I try it on a vector (below) it applies the function to each element in the vector one by one.
<!-- USE THE CODE CHUNK BELOW IF YOU'D LIKE -->
```{r Question 3a}
cents <- 1:10
get_minimum_coins(cents)
```

### (b)
<!-- ENTER YOUR ANSWER BELOW, IT CAN BE JUST COMMANDs; NO NEED TO STORE OBJECTs -->
```{r Question 3b}
which(get_minimum_coins(1:100) == max(get_minimum_coins(1:100)))
```

## Question 4

### (a)
<!-- CREATE THE FUNCTION IN THE CODE CHUNK BELOW -->
<!-- NAME THE FUNCTION AND ITS INPUTS EXACTLY AS STATED IN THE ASSIGNENT -->
<!-- PLAN OUT YOUR APPROACH BEFORE YOU START CODING ANY FUNCTION. -->
```{r Question 4a}

my_min <- function(x, na.rm = FALSE){
  if (na.rm){
    x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  }
  
  min <- x[1]
  
    for (n in x) {
      if (is.na(n)) {
        min <- NA
        break
      }
      if (n <= min) {
        min <- n
      }
      
    }
  min
  }
```

### (b)
<!-- USE THE CODE CHUNK BELOW, IT CAN BE JUST COMMANDs; NO NEED TO STORE OBJECTs -->
```{r Question 4b}
my_min(c(4, 1, 0, 2, -3, -5, -4))
my_min(c("bears", "beets", "Battlestar Galactica"))
my_min(7)
my_min(c("Pawnee", "rules", "Eagleton", NA), na.rm = TRUE)
my_min(c("Pawnee", "rules", "Eagleton", NA))     
my_min(NA, na.rm = TRUE)       
my_min(NA, na.rm = FALSE)       

```

## Question 7

### (a)
<!-- CREATE THE FUNCTION IN THE CODE CHUNK BELOW -->
<!-- NAME THE FUNCTION AND ITS INPUTS EXACTLY AS STATED IN THE ASSIGNENT -->
<!-- PLAN OUT YOUR APPROACH BEFORE YOU START CODING ANY FUNCTION. -->
```{r Question 7a}
my_ifelse <- function(test,yes,no) {
  output <- 0
  output[which(test)] <- yes[which(test)]
  output[which(!test)] <- no[which(!test)]
  output
}
```

### (b)
<!-- USE THE CODE CHUNK BELOW -->
```{r Question 7b}
x <- (1:10) * pi
my_ifelse(x %% 1 >= 0.5, x %/% 1 + 1, x %/% 1)
```

### (c)
<!-- CREATE THE FUNCTIONs IN THE CODE CHUNK BELOW -->
<!-- NAME THE FUNCTIONs AND THEIR INPUTS EXACTLY AS STATED IN THE ASSIGNENT -->
<!-- PLAN OUT YOUR APPROACH BEFORE YOU START CODING ANY FUNCTION. -->
```{r Question 7c}
my_abs <- function(x) {
  my_ifelse(x >= 0, x, -x)
}

my_sign <- function(x) {
  result <- my_ifelse(x > 0, x/x, -x/x)
  result[which(is.nan(result))] <- 0
  result
}

```
<!-- REMINDER TO USE my_ifelse() TO WRITE THE FUNCTIONS. THERE ARE OTHER WAYS TO WRITE THESE FUNCTIONS WITHOUT USING my_ifelse() BUT PLEASE FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS. -->

## Question 8

### (a)
<!-- CREATE THE FUNCTIONs IN THE CODE CHUNK BELOW -->
<!-- NAME THE FUNCTIONs AND THEIR INPUTS EXACTLY AS STATED IN THE ASSIGNENT -->
<!-- PLAN OUT YOUR APPROACH BEFORE YOU START CODING ANY FUNCTION. -->
```{r Question 8a}
merge <- function(left,right) {
  merged <- 0
  while (length(left) > 0) {
    if (length(right) > 0) {
      if (left[1] < right[1]) {
        merged <- c(merged,left[i])
        left <- left[-1]
      } else {
        merged <- c(merged,right[i])
        right <- right[-1]}
    } else {
      merged <- c(merged,left)
      left <- 0}
  }
  c(merged,right)
}

merge_sort <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) > 1) {
    half <- length(x)/2
    left <- x[1:half]
    right <- x[half+1:length(x)]
    sorted_left <- merge_sort(left)
    sorted_right <- merge_sort(right)
    x <- merge(sorted_left, sorted_right)
  }
  x
}
```
